quick: Individualized; e.g., start 75-150 IU FSH SC/IM daily, titrate by ovarian response

summary: Urofollitropin is a purified preparation of human follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) extracted from the urine of postmenopausal women. It stimulates ovarian follicular development for ovulation induction and controlled ovarian stimulation in assisted reproductive technology, and can support spermatogenesis in men with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism. Therapy must be individualized and closely monitored to avoid ovarian hyperstimulation and multiple pregnancy.
indications: Stimulation of multiple follicular development (controlled ovarian stimulation) for assisted reproductive technology programs
Ovulation induction in women with anovulation or oligo-ovulation, including polycystic ovary syndrome, who have not responded to clomifene citrate
With human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG), stimulation of spermatogenesis in men with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (per product-specific labeling)

dosage.d: Individualized; commonly start 75 to 150 IU FSH daily, adjust by 37.5 IU steps no more often than every 7 days based on response; hCG given to trigger ovulation when follicles mature
dosage.t: Once daily injection; lowest effective dose
dosage.n: Step-up regimen to find the FSH threshold while minimizing OHSS and multiple gestation

dosage.d: Individualized starting dose (e.g., 150-225 IU daily) within a pituitary down-regulation or antagonist protocol; titrate by follicular response
dosage.n: Dose and protocol set by the reproductive specialist

dosage.d: Per product labeling, typically after hCG pretreatment, given several times weekly for months
dosage.n: Long courses needed to induce spermatogenesis

admin: Administer by subcutaneous or intramuscular injection as directed; reconstitute lyophilized powder immediately before use
Initiate and supervise treatment only by physicians experienced in infertility management
Monitor ovarian response with serum estradiol and transvaginal ultrasound before each dose escalation and before the hCG trigger
Withhold the hCG trigger and counsel on barrier contraception if there is excessive ovarian response (risk of OHSS)
Rotate injection sites; subcutaneous self-injection may be taught to the patient
moa: Urofollitropin contains follicle-stimulating hormone that binds FSH receptors on ovarian granulosa cells, promoting recruitment and growth of ovarian follicles and increasing estradiol production. Final follicular maturation and ovulation are then triggered by human chorionic gonadotropin, which mimics the luteinizing hormone surge. In men, FSH acts on Sertoli cells to support spermatogenesis when testosterone is provided by hCG.

absolute: Tumors of the pituitary, hypothalamus, ovary, uterus, or breast (or testis in men)
Ovarian cysts or enlargement not due to polycystic ovary syndrome
relative: Prior excessive ovarian response or OHSS
Conditions in which pregnancy is hazardous
monitor: Follicular size and number on ultrasound
Symptoms and signs of ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome

preg: Urofollitropin is contraindicated in pregnancy. It is used only to achieve pregnancy; once conception occurs the drug is stopped. There is no benefit, and gonadotropins should not be administered to a pregnant woman.
lact: Urofollitropin is not indicated during breastfeeding. There is no role for ovarian stimulation during lactation, and use is not recommended.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment for renal impairment has been established. Use under specialist supervision.
hepatic: No specific dosage adjustment for hepatic impairment has been established. Use under specialist supervision.

major: Human chorionic gonadotropin (used intentionally to trigger ovulation; can increase OHSS risk)
moderate: Clomifene citrate (may potentiate ovarian response when used sequentially or together)
minor: No clinically significant drug-drug interactions are well characterized
interactions.diagnostics: Raises serum estradiol; interpret hormone assays in the context of the stimulation cycle

emergency: Severe OHSS (rapid weight gain, severe abdominal pain and swelling, decreased urination, shortness of breath) - seek emergency care
Sudden severe one-sided pelvic pain (ovarian torsion) - emergency care
Signs of blood clot (leg swelling/pain, chest pain, breathlessness) - emergency care

monitoring: Serum estradiol before dose escalation and before the hCG trigger
Transvaginal ultrasound to count and measure developing follicles
Symptoms and signs of ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome
Weight, abdominal girth, and urine output if OHSS is suspected
Pregnancy outcome and number of gestational sacs
counsel: This medicine is given by injection, often self-administered after training, to help your ovaries produce eggs
Keep all monitoring appointments for blood tests and scans so the dose can be adjusted safely
Report severe abdominal pain or swelling, rapid weight gain, reduced urination, or trouble breathing - these may signal overstimulation
Be aware of the increased chance of twins or higher multiples
Use the dose and timing exactly as your fertility specialist instructs
pk: Follicular growth develops over days of repeated dosing
Serum FSH peaks within hours of subcutaneous/intramuscular injection
Elimination half-life of FSH approximately 24-37 hours
Cumulative effect over the stimulation cycle; ovulation triggered by hCG
Store per product labeling, typically refrigerated or at controlled room temperature; reconstitute just before use
pearls: FDA-approval status varies by region; dosing and indications here follow EMA/SmPC and BNF sources
Purified urinary FSH; final follicular maturation and ovulation are triggered separately by hCG
Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome and multiple pregnancy are the principal risks - use the lowest effective dose with close ultrasound and estradiol monitoring
Step-up dosing identifies the individual FSH threshold, especially in polycystic ovary syndrome
Withhold the hCG trigger if there is excessive follicular response
missed: If a daily injection is missed, contact your fertility clinic for advice rather than doubling the dose; the team may adjust the schedule. Correct timing relative to monitoring and the hCG trigger is important.
overdose: The main consequence of excessive dosing is ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome. Management is supportive, including withholding further gonadotropin and hCG, monitoring for fluid shifts and thromboembolism, and hospital care for severe cases. Seek specialist and emergency care for severe OHSS.
